scope: Editorial checks fixed after the AM selection-v3 originals were frozen and before this final-policy writer response; development case, not an independent final-policy held-out date.

central_checks.topic: Completed US session and stale background
central_checks.check: Use the 22 September US close for today's S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite, including the Nasdaq rise versus flat/slightly lower S&P and falling Dow. The large all-index gains in the 21 September articles are previous-session context, not today's return. Do not add unsourced breadth or mix the two sessions.

Explain AI/selected technology leadership and material laggards such as consumer-app or ride-hailing names when they change the claim of market-wide strength. Separate observed moves from causal inference.

central_checks.topic: Iran diplomacy, energy and opposed risk
central_checks.check: Distinguish a three-hour US-Iran meeting with no confirmed deal, the reported conditional seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal, US threats/sanction steps and Iranian military retaliation. Use the 22 September oil close where available and keep the preceding 21 September oil move dated. A diesel export ban is under examination, not enacted. Explain which energy and Korean exposures could change and what would disconfirm the risk or relief reading.

central_checks.topic: Monetary policy baseline and scope of Fed statements
central_checks.check: If Fed warnings are material, state the reported current 3.75-4.00% range, latest 0.25 percentage-point increase and 4.1% year-end dot-plot median as a projection. Collins/Barkin discuss inflation and possible policy restraint; Williams discusses rate-control operating tools, not a rate-cut signal. Do not flatten these different scopes into one firm policy decision. Use the Korean central-bank rate-burden estimate only with its conditional basis and horizon.

Mention the sourced dollar rise as a previous-session observation, not a fabricated current USD/KRW close. The supplied SBS article links this week's US-China summit to the next market checkpoint but does not establish an exact release time; avoid inventing one. State why either would matter for Korean exposure, with appropriate uncertainty.

failure_rules: Unsupported close, session, price basis, binding-policy or agreement claim is a factual failure.
Omitting a conclusion-changing Iran counterproposal, active Fed baseline or near-term trade checkpoint fails substantive coverage even if included claims are true.
A long headline list without economic transmission, opposing evidence and observable next checks is not a substantive brief.
